items.title: International media voice alarm over Israel's arrest of West Bank journalist
items.description:
The group representing international media in Israel and the Palestinian territories voiced alarm on Monday over Israeli forces’ arrest of an Agence France-Presse (AFP) freelancer in the West Bank, urging his release unless evidence is presented.
The Foreign Press Association (FPA) expressed “deep concern” over the arrest in a pre-dawn raid on Sunday of Mohammad Ateeq, a video contributor for the international news agency around the northern city of Jenin.
“The army says he is ‘suspected of terror ties’, but it has given no evidence, filed no charges and held him incommunicado,” it said.

items.title: I made Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad take the 10-minute park test
items.description:
The ten-minute park test asks whether people can reach a public park or playground on foot from their homes. Its purpose is to identify neighbourhoods without everyday access to recreation and help direct investment towards them. In its population-based form, the score is the proportion of residents living within that walking distance. It tells us something that the amount of green on a satellite image cannot: whether public open space is within reach of the people who need it.

items.title: Symbol of neglect
items.description:
NOTHING quite prepares you for the sensory overload you experience when you move from the pristine and polished Islamabad to the battered and potholed Karachi.
To the discerning eye, Karachi looks like a low-resolution version of Islamabad, that too in sepia tones.
The vibrancy of the “City of Lights” is mellowed by the haze of suspended smoke and dust, further muted by the drabness of its infrastructure. Its skyline, characterised by decrepit buildings woven through a not-so-intricate web of overhead wires, pales in comparison with Islamabad’s lush green, hilly landscape.

items.description:

items.title: US airports slowly return to normal after 3 days of disruption
items.description:
US air travel was slowly returning to normal on Monday after three days of widespread disruption following an extraordinary no-takeoff order issued by US aviation authorities.
The ground stop issued Friday afternoon was only the second time such a directive had been issued nationwide in the busy US airspace since planes were grounded following the 9/11 attacks, and was blamed by the Trump administration on a faulty upgrade to communications equipment.
On Monday morning, more than 250 US-related flights — those travelling within, into or out of the US — scheduled for the same day were cancelled

items.title: Ex-Bangladesh PM Hasina to return home despite 'threat of death'
items.description:
